note: Generic CCTV safety decision questions written before any API call; not derived from benchmark samples. Frozen with freeze/p1_freeze.json.
policy: Use only the supplied computer-vision observations. Do not assume a medical diagnosis. Do not infer criminal intent. Do not infer authorization or lack of authorization. Do not infer identity. Do not infer weapons unless supported by supplied evidence. Treat null/unavailable fields as unknown, not false. Treat low-reliability CV proxies (reliability "limited") as uncertain evidence. Confidence and risk are separate concepts.

scope.single: Consider the observations of the single supplied camera.
scope.camera: Consider only the observations for camera {camera}; ignore the other cameras for this question.
scope.multi_camera: Consider the observations from all supplied cameras together. Camera clips are not synchronized and person identity across cameras is not established.

per_assessment_questions.instructions: Does the provided CV evidence indicate a safety-relevant incident or condition that should be surfaced to a CCTV operator?
Which generic category best describes the most safety-relevant pattern in the CV observations?

choices.description: Observations show ordinary presence or movement with no safety-relevant pattern.
A person shows a transition to, or prolonged, low or horizontal posture.
Two or more people show sustained close proximity together with rapid relative movement or limb-motion proxies.
A person enters, appears in, or moves across the scene in a way an operator may want to check; boundary semantics are not known.
Another safety-relevant pattern not covered by the other categories.
The observations are too unreliable or ambiguous to choose a category.

per_assessment_questions.instructions: How severe is the potential harm suggested by the observed pattern, if it is what it appears to be?

levels.label: moderate
levels.description: Possible injury or harm that warrants attention.

levels.label: serious
levels.description: Likely injury or serious harm to a person.

levels.label: critical
levels.description: Potentially life-threatening or very serious harm.

per_assessment_questions.instructions: How urgently does a CCTV operator need to look at this camera now?

levels.label: immediate
levels.description: Needs attention right now; the condition is ongoing at the end of the observation.

per_assessment_questions.instructions: Based on the observable number of people and the extent of the pattern, how many people are involved in or exposed to it?

levels.label: small_group
levels.description: Three or four people involved or nearby.

levels.label: many
levels.description: Five or more people or a wide area involved.

per_assessment_questions.instructions: How long does the observed incident-like pattern persist over the sampled observation window?

levels.label: momentary
levels.description: Seen in one or two samples only.

levels.label: sustained
levels.description: Persists for a large part of the remaining observation.

levels.label: ongoing
levels.description: Persists until the end of the observation.

per_assessment_questions.instructions: Should a human CCTV operator review this candidate because of either risk or uncertainty?

attention_questions.instructions: These cameras are presented as concurrent alerts. Considering the observations of all cameras, which camera most needs a CCTV operator's attention first?

choices.description: No camera clearly needs attention before the others.

multi_camera_questions.instructions: Do the supplied camera-level CV observation patterns support the interpretation that the cameras may be observing the same underlying incident? Do not assume identity or synchronization has been confirmed.
Does the second camera view add useful evidence beyond what the best single camera view provides?
How much evidential value does combining the camera views add?

levels.label: very_high
levels.description: The combined views are essential to understand the situation.

adapter.refused_score_note: uninformative midpoint used only because prediction.schema.json requires a number; flagged in uncertainties and forces human review
adapter.confidence_formula: mean of available [incident_category.confidence, max(p_incident, 1 - p_incident)]; multiplied by 0.5 if any of these two answers is a refusal; 0.0 if both refused

event_type_map.possible_scene_or_boundary_entry: possible scene or boundary entry (boundary semantics unknown)
